extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification. The dataset is released in RGB and multi-spectral (MS) versions. Image patches measure 64x64 pixels.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.publisher: TU Kaiserslautern, German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
extraction.citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., & Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were acquired from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Images were selected that were associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected, and images recorded throughout the year were included to capture high intra-class variance. From these satellite images, 27,000 georeferenced image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted and manually checked.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite images from the ESA Copernicus Earth observation program, downloaded via Amazon S3. Images cover 34 European countries (Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy/Holy See, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Macedonia, Malta, Republic of Moldova, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Ukraine and United Kingdom).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution have been upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation for single-band image evaluation. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images were selected with low cloud levels using ESA-provided cloud level values. Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite images. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 10 land use and land cover classes were chosen based on the principle that they were visible at the resolution of 10 meters per pixel and were frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas. The composition of individual classes and their relationships follows the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times to correct ground truth labels.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The classification system opens a gate towards Earth observation applications including land use and land cover change detection, urban area development monitoring, nature protection, sustainable development, detection of deforestation (a main contributor to climate change, e.g., to notice illegal clearing of forests), and assistance in keeping geographical maps (such as OpenStreetMap) up-to-date.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution of images is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. There is a low positive correlation between classes; the classes most similar to each other are the two agricultural classes and the two classes representing residential and industrial buildings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. A classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The classifier sometimes confuses the agricultural land classes as well as the classes highway and river.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for land use and land cover classification using deep Convolutional Neural Networks. Applications include land use and land cover change detection, and assistance in improving geographical maps (e.g., OpenStreetMap). Can be used as a basis for large-scale training of deep neural networks for satellite image classification.
